Q: C/C++ : why variables in main() are on the stack? A:

C doesn't specify working with the stack or sections like .data. Variables have storage duration - in your case you're talking about automatic vs static storage duration. It's an implementation detail that compilers use the stack for automatic and a fixed location such as .data (or .rodata or whatever) for static.

The storage duration of variables is given by the code you write. Just because main() is the entry point for your program doesn't lead to interpreting code in it differently from any other function.

The answer to your "why?" is: because you told it to.

Q: Is there a JavaScript API to trigger the browser-native "Split Screen" feature A:

This feature is a proposal by the Microsoft Edge development team. You can find their proposal on their GitHub. Their proposal is this:

  • HTML Anchor element

    <a target="_split" href="https://www.example.com">Open in split tab</a>

  • window.open API

    // Open url in split tab.
window.open("https://www.example.com", "_split");

As of April 2026 this feature is still a proposal.

Q: Does Jax's JIT compiler unroll for loops inside if statements that are not executed? A:

I don't know the answer to your question, but I don't think that the motivation for asking it is sound. It boils down to this:

"Unrolling the loop would be undesirable because it could massively increase the compile time."

  1. JIT compile time should be irrelevant. The code should be compiled once and then executed many times. If you are repeatedly JIT compiling the same code multiple times, something is wrong: doing that would be inefficient.

  2. The cost of JIT compilation (of an unrolled loop) shouldn't be "massive".

  3. If (in spite of 1 and 2) there is a real (i.e. you have measured it!) performance issue here, then there is a simple work-around. Tune your code. In your example, you could move the for loop into a separate function, and JIT compile it separately ... or not.

Before you try 3, make sure that you understand how to measure your application properly (the jax.jit documentation uses timeit in its examples) and methodically do before and after tests for each tuning tweak that you make.

Also, be aware that the behavior of the JAX JIT compiler could be version dependent, and you may need to redo the tuning for different versions.

Having said the above, as I was reading the jax.jit documentation, I came across this section:

  • https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/jit-compilation.html#why-can-t-we-just-jit-everything

You should read that carefully. In that it says:

"Traced values within JIT, like x and n here, can only affect control flow via their static attributes: such as shape or dtype, and not via their values."

I think that means that in your example where do_the_loop is a runtime variable, the JIT compiler would not take account of value of that variable in deciding whether or not to unroll the loop.

But as I said above, I don't think it matters. Time to JIT compile should not have a significant bearing on overall performance ... if you are using it correctly.

Q: SAP ABAP CL_SALV_TABLE column optimization not working A:

Here's a minimal reproducible example that demonstrates the column optimization:

REPORT z_alv_optimize_columns.
PARAMETERS dummy.
AT SELECTION-SCREEN OUTPUT.
  DATA go_salv TYPE REF TO cl_salv_table.

  IF go_salv IS NOT BOUND.
    SELECT *
      FROM sflight
      INTO TABLE @DATA(gt_sflight).
    cl_salv_table=>factory( EXPORTING r_container  = cl_gui_container=>screen0
                            IMPORTING r_salv_table = go_salv
                            CHANGING  t_table      = gt_sflight ).
    go_salv->get_columns( )->set_optimize( abap_true ).
    go_salv->display( ).
  ENDIF.

Q: Confused about C++ linkage A:

On Posix-like system a static lib is indeed an archive made by ar utility. What is used on Windows is totally toolchain-dependant, static libs don't have an universal format there, DLLs do (kinda, still can be ABI problems).

Q: RealityKit Complains "Could not locate file 'default-binaryarchive.metallib' in bundle." A:

Try adding the RealityKit &/or Metal framework manually

Target > General > Frameworks, Libraries & Embedded Content > + > Select Framework > Add

IDK why it is happening but I have seen missing frameworks a couple of times.
